source_text: Brutes rely on physical strength and melee weapons to strike down foes. Primary attribute: Physical
Adepts have natural abilities in casting magical spells. Primary attribute: Mental
Scouts specialize in range weaponry and combat accuracy. Primary attribute: Offense
Keepers focus on defensive powers for survival. Primary attribute: Defense
Wanderers choose their own paths. Primary attribute: custom
The seams on this hood are designed to aid the flow of mana.
Frost resistance runes line the inside of this vest.
The fire resistance runes that hem these sleeves help protect beginner students of Pyromancy.
Spell components are tucked into hidden pockets covering this skirt.
Attunement with the elements allow mages to ice and fire walk.
This nondescript ring was forged in the land where shadows lie.
These enchanted boots are prized possessions of Courier guildsmen.
In Lower Sceleris there is honor among thieves. Everyone else is a mark.
Use: Blink to a nearby location
The secrets to harvesting Yggdrasil twigs are known only to traitorous dryads.
The workmanship on this blade appears hurried, as if forged under the fever of vigilance.
Faded memories are vivid to the wearer of this silver band.
This tome bears the seal of the Averguard
Opens special doors in Averguard Keep
Tho' Nature, red in tooth and claw; With ravine, shriek'd against his creed
"Some say the Averguard Academy is the greatest collection of knowledge within the empire."
"Professor Langlier is High Sage of the Averguard.  Several volumes kept here are his own writings."
"The Academy is only open to oathkeeping members of the Averguard.  Few others know of its existence."
"The peasants could not be trusted with literacy.  Most gave up their books without incident."
This false book has a secret compartment.
This tomb glows with magical runes.
This book is entitled "Training Your Antlion". Chapter 1 is "How Not To Get Eaten". The rest of the book is unfinished.
The last entry of this well-preserved journal reads: "I feared it would come to this.  I knew the Warden's secrets but they would not be contained forever."
You insert the Averguard Key. Runes glow around the door, then fade. The door is still sealed.
You read aloud the runes on Langlier's Talisman. The Avergard Key begins to glow!
"Some said Sir Maddox cared too much for the peasants.  He would not quarantine, saying the villagers did not deserve to die locked away."
"Maddox died of the plague in 638.  After attempts to magically revive him failed he was sealed deep behind the temple."
A plaque under the statue reads "Sir Evan Maddox, may he return to rescue us all"
A ghastly voice reverberates from the next chamber.  "What fool disturbs my tomb?!"
You wipe dust away from the tomb lid, revealing an inscription: "Here lies Sir Evan Maddox"
A locked gate is here, with a small keyhole in the center.

"Today Pompeii got a little over-excited to meet me and blew himself up. So I had to go into the caves and catch myself a NEW antlion burster. Again. I think I'm going to name this one 'Krakatoa'. ~Vesuvvio (the Destroyer)"
"When we could no longer stand the idiotic practices of our master, I hatched a plan to kill him. My brothers agreed the deed had to be done."

"In accordance with our plan, G. asked the old fool to teach him about the preparation of corpses in the later stages of decay. Naturally, the corpse in question was a cleverly disguised bomb made by V."

"My brothers and I wandered around for a few days. In an incredible stroke of luck, we encountered a master necromancer who, seeing the marks of banishment on our foreheads, took us as his apprentices."
"We grew swiftly under the tutelage of the necromancer. The more we learned, the more we realized we could do better than the short-sighted git."
"My brothers V. and G. used to go to a wizard's academy with me. We were top students until one day V. killed another student in a spontaneous fit of rage."

"Naturally, V. was expelled for his crime. It was foolish of us, but G. and I decided to defend our brother. We were expelled too. The wizards magically marked us with a sign of banishment on our foreheads so that no wizard would dare teach us."
"G. suggested that each of us should take one of the halls in the old necromancer's lair."
"It's days like today that make me wonder if I should go a step further and eliminate V. and G. too... they're getting on my nerves. ~Scathelocke"
"Fire is either Falling or Waiting. One element, one temperament."
"Wind is not Rising. Wind is Falling on the firmament."
"People used to ask me why I use a sword rather than a wand. It never occurs to them that the metal blade can conduct and channel lightning as well as (or better than!) any enchanted twig. ~Grisbon"
The crumbling walls of the south tunnel are held up by planks of rotting wood.
These goblins have captured a human trader.  Human bones are carefully arranged around the pillar in preparation for a goblin ritual.
Talrych says, "You arrived just in time.  Please, take this."
The walls collapse inward and rubble blocks off the passage!
This pillar is laced with cracks and crevices. Maybe with enough force it can be knocked down.
Run! You don't want to be caught in the blast of your own explosion!
This book bears the seal of the Averguard
"In the Age of Settlement, the Averguard Knights defended peasants against the chaos of the wilderness."
"Sir Evan Maddox led the Averguard when the plague struck.  Powerful clerics from the corners of the world were brought here.  By the time a cure was found it was too late."
It looks like the necromancer has been raising the corpses of dead miners as his minions.
A natural underground river flows through this room.
The river appears to have swollen recently, covering the location where the tracks once were.
The undead in this room are dressed in the remnants of shredded mining clothes.
You spot the abandoned tower in the distance.
Looking through the grate, you confirm the tower is empty.
I am Guill, a scribe with the Order. I am grateful you've come -- we are short on trained warriors due to the call-to-arms in Ancelot.
context: npc_name=Guill, Scribe of the Order; utterance_role=npc; set_status=ak_intro; requires_not_status=ak_maddox_reward

source_text: Why is the Order interested in these ruins?
context: npc_name=Guill, Scribe of the Order; utterance_role=player; set_status=ak_intro; requires_not_status=ak_maddox_reward

source_text: What the locals call the Goblin Warrens is actually the entrance to a grand underground fortress known as Averguard Keep. This site is sacred to our order. Our primary mission is to cleanse the evil from this place.
context: npc_name=Guill, Scribe of the Order; utterance_role=npc; set_status=ak_intro; requires_not_status=ak_maddox_reward

source_text: The goblins in the Warrens answer to a warlord named Ukkonen. Most goblins are merely curious; this Ukkonen is bloodthirsty. Punish him for desecrating this place. His lair is here in the Warrens.
context: npc_name=Guill, Scribe of the Order; utterance_role=npc; requires_status=ak_intro; requires_not_status=ak_ukkonen_search; set_status=ak_ukkonen_search; unset_status=ak_ukkonen_defeated

source_text: Ukkonen's lair is somewhere here in the Goblin Warrens.
context: npc_name=Guill, Scribe of the Order; utterance_role=npc; requires_status=ak_ukkonen_search; requires_not_status=ak_ukkonen_defeated

source_text: Ukkonen is defeated -- I sensed a calm in this place the moment you ended him. Take this reward for your bravery.
context: npc_name=Guill, Scribe of the Order; utterance_role=npc; requires_status=ak_ukkonen_search; requires_status=ak_ukkonen_defeated; requires_not_status=ak_ukkonen_reward; set_status=ak_ukkonen_reward

source_text: The Averguard left a set of Chronicles detailing their final era. One volume is missing. I've searched this entire area except for Ukkonen's lair. If you find the book please return to me.
context: npc_name=Guill, Scribe of the Order; utterance_role=npc; requires_status=ak_intro; requires_not_status=ak_tome_found; set_status=ak_tome_search

source_text: I'll keep an eye out for it.
context: npc_name=Guill, Scribe of the Order; utterance_role=player; requires_status=ak_intro; requires_not_status=ak_tome_found; set_status=ak_tome_search

source_text: You found this tome in Ukkonen's lair? Most excellent -- I feared this volume was lost. With it we can piece together the true history of this keep. I just need a moment to study...
context: npc_name=Guill, Scribe of the Order; utterance_role=npc; requires_status=ak_tome_found; requires_item=9000; set_status=ak_tome_reward

source_text: This tome confirms what we know of Averguard Keep -- it crumbled against the plague many centuries ago. But not all of the infected were destroyed. It appears many undead where locked away in hopes that a cure would be found.
context: npc_name=Guill, Scribe of the Order; utterance_role=npc; requires_status=ak_tome_reward; requires_not_status=ak_key_found; set_status=ak_key_search
npc_name=Guill, Scribe of the Order; utterance_role=player; requires_status=ak_tome_reward; requires_not_status=ak_key_found; set_status=ak_key_search

source_text: I don't know, but we should investigate. Head into the Atrium, then the Averguard Prison. Search for a key to access the sealed areas of the Keep.
context: npc_name=Guill, Scribe of the Order; utterance_role=npc; requires_status=ak_tome_reward; requires_not_status=ak_key_found; set_status=ak_key_search

source_text: I have the prison key. The old prison warden carried it on his person -- he was infected, haunting the depths of the Prison.
context: npc_name=Guill, Scribe of the Order; utterance_role=player; requires_not_status=ak_key_reward; requires_status=ak_key_found; requires_item=9001; set_status=ak_key_reward

source_text: A true shame that he was infected.  Well, now that we have the Averguard Key, the depths of Averguard Keep are open to us. The Order thanks you.
context: npc_name=Guill, Scribe of the Order; utterance_role=npc; requires_not_status=ak_key_reward; requires_status=ak_key_found; requires_item=9001; set_status=ak_key_reward

source_text: There is one place within the Keep that no living being has seen for centuries: the burial chamber behind Averguard Temple. From the Atrium you can access the Temple. Use your key to enter the Burial Chamber.
context: npc_name=Guill, Scribe of the Order; utterance_role=npc; requires_status=ak_key_reward; requires_not_status=ak_temple_sealed; requires_not_status=ak_talisman_used; set_status=ak_temple_search
npc_name=Guill, Scribe of the Order; utterance_role=player; requires_status=ak_key_reward; requires_not_status=ak_temple_sealed; requires_not_status=ak_talisman_used; set_status=ak_temple_search

source_text: The powerful leader of the Averguard -- Sir Evan Maddox.
context: npc_name=Guill, Scribe of the Order; utterance_role=npc; requires_status=ak_key_reward; requires_not_status=ak_temple_sealed; requires_not_status=ak_talisman_used; set_status=ak_temple_search

source_text: I tried the key on the Burial Chamber door but it would not open.
context: npc_name=Guill, Scribe of the Order; utterance_role=player; requires_not_status=ak_talisman_found; requires_status=ak_temple_sealed; set_status=ak_talisman_search

source_text: It must be sealed by powerful magic. There was only one sorceror of Averguard with that kind of power - Professor Langlier. Search through his collection to find a way into the Burial Chamber. Enter the Academy through the Atrium.
context: npc_name=Guill, Scribe of the Order; utterance_role=npc; requires_not_status=ak_talisman_found; requires_status=ak_temple_sealed; set_status=ak_talisman_search
npc_name=Guill, Scribe of the Order; utterance_role=player; requires_not_status=ak_talisman_found; requires_status=ak_temple_sealed; set_status=ak_talisman_search

source_text: I must admit jealousy -- I have dreamed many years of seeing the old volumes there, but it is simply too dangerous yet.
context: npc_name=Guill, Scribe of the Order; utterance_role=npc; requires_not_status=ak_talisman_found; requires_status=ak_temple_sealed; set_status=ak_talisman_search

source_text: I am back from the Academy. Langlier was rags and bones, yet still a powerful mage. He wore this symbol.
context: npc_name=Guill, Scribe of the Order; utterance_role=player; requires_status=ak_talisman_found; requires_not_status=ak_talisman_reward; requires_item=9002; set_status=ak_talisman_reward

source_text: Fate has delivered this talisman to you. With it and the Averguard Key, you have the ability to open the Burial Chamber. Read these runes aloud at the sealed door and the path will be opened.
context: npc_name=Guill, Scribe of the Order; utterance_role=npc; requires_status=ak_talisman_found; requires_not_status=ak_talisman_reward; requires_item=9002; set_status=ak_talisman_reward

source_text: My worst fear is come alive. Just as with the Warden and with Professor Langlier, Sir Evan Maddox himself was inflicted with undeath. If we are to reclaim the Keep, you must defeat him. The Order will reward you magnificently for this service. But be prepared -- not even undeath will limit Maddox's zeal. Enter the Burial Chamber and allow him redemption.
context: npc_name=Guill, Scribe of the Order; utterance_role=npc; requires_not_status=ak_maddox_defeated; requires_status=ak_key_found; requires_status=ak_talisman_found; set_status=ak_maddox_search

source_text: You have risked much for the Order. Take this final reward, as your mission here is complete. The grip of necromancy over Averguard Keep is broken -- in time the remaining undead will pass over into death.
context: npc_name=Guill, Scribe of the Order; utterance_role=npc; requires_status=ak_maddox_defeated; requires_status=ak_key_reward; requires_status=ak_talisman_reward; requires_not_status=ak_maddox_reward; set_status=ak_maddox_reward

source_text: Thank you Guill. I am glad to be of service.
context: npc_name=Guill, Scribe of the Order; utterance_role=player; requires_status=ak_maddox_defeated; requires_status=ak_key_reward; requires_status=ak_talisman_reward; requires_not_status=ak_maddox_reward; set_status=ak_maddox_reward

source_text: It is still dangerous here, but with Maddox defeated his followers will soon find rest.
context: npc_name=Guill, Scribe of the Order; utterance_role=npc; requires_status=ak_maddox_reward

source_text: Welcome to my mines, stranger. If you have the back for it, I've got the work.
context: npc_name=Martigan, Overseer; utterance_role=npc; requires_not_status=ml_skeleton_search; set_status=ml_skeleton_search; unset_status=ml_skeleton_defeated

source_text: I heard you might have something more interesting.
context: npc_name=Martigan, Overseer; utterance_role=player; requires_not_status=ml_skeleton_search; set_status=ml_skeleton_search; unset_status=ml_skeleton_defeated

source_text: Ah, you're the adventurer? If you seek out danger you're in the right place. We had two guards stationed here; both were recalled to Ancelot. Now we're vulnerable.
context: npc_name=Martigan, Overseer; utterance_role=npc; requires_not_status=ml_skeleton_search; set_status=ml_skeleton_search; unset_status=ml_skeleton_defeated
npc_name=Martigan, Overseer; utterance_role=player; requires_not_status=ml_skeleton_search; set_status=ml_skeleton_search; unset_status=ml_skeleton_defeated

source_text: Not good at all. While I was digging, my pickaxe scraped a skull that was wedged in the rock wall. Before I knew it, the nasty thing started moving and a whole body emerged. Now that thing is in there, preventing any more mining.
context: npc_name=Martigan, Overseer; utterance_role=npc; requires_not_status=ml_skeleton_search; set_status=ml_skeleton_search; unset_status=ml_skeleton_defeated

source_text: Kill that skeleton for me, and I'll make it worth your while.
context: npc_name=Martigan, Overseer; utterance_role=npc; requires_not_status=ml_skeleton_search; set_status=ml_skeleton_search; unset_status=ml_skeleton_defeated

source_text: We're having problems. Goblins. All the noise from our mining is drawing their attention. We can't have them thinking we're easy prey.
context: npc_name=Martigan, Overseer; utterance_role=npc; requires_status=ml_skeleton_reward; requires_not_status=fr_rilrak_search; set_status=fr_rilrak_search; unset_status=fr_rilrak_defeated

source_text: Attack their encampment up river from here. 20 gold now, 80 more when you return.
context: npc_name=Martigan, Overseer; utterance_role=npc; requires_status=ml_skeleton_reward; requires_not_status=fr_rilrak_search; set_status=fr_rilrak_search; unset_status=fr_rilrak_defeated

source_text: The goblins have an encampment up the river from here on the west side. Clear them out and I'll pay you 80 gold.
Unfortunate work, but my workers will sleep safe tonight. Here's your reward.
context: npc_name=Martigan, Overseer; utterance_role=npc; requires_status=fr_rilrak_search; requires_status=fr_rilrak_defeated; requires_not_status=fr_rilrak_reward; set_status=fr_rilrak_reward

source_text: A member of the Order passed through our camp a few days ago. He left for the tower ruins in Ydrakka Pass.
This region was once well guarded. There are watch towers positioned throughout these plains, but most are abandoned and crumbling now.
context: npc_name=Martigan, Overseer; utterance_role=npc; requires_status=ml_skeleton_reward; requires_not_status=rotten_tower_search; set_status=rotten_tower_search

source_text: I need someone to inspect the outpost tower in White Winds, south west of the Frontier Plains. Let me know if goblins have found their way inside.
context: npc_name=Martigan, Overseer; utterance_role=npc; requires_status=ml_skeleton_reward; requires_not_status=rotten_tower_search; set_status=rotten_tower_search

source_text: Search for the abandoned tower southwest of the Frontier plains. The lands around there are called White Wind.
There are plenty of goblins in the White Winds area, but not near the tower.
Are you sure? Did you look inside the tower?
There are plenty of goblins in the white winds area, but not near the tower.

The dig near Perdition Harbor is starting to show promise. We found ruins. Unlike anything else in the area. We'll get a good amount of gold from the relics here. A welcome change for the guys that transferred from the Empyrean's operation in the complex under Lochport.
They told me about the other expeditions, a tower in Black Oak City and a temple in the Stormrock region. Both just as fruitless.
Today, we found a peculiar yellow-green mineral. Almost blinding to look at. Perhaps someone from the Empyrean Chamber knows what it is...

The messenger to the Chamber called the mineral "Mastite". It was made clear that any we find must be brought to the surface. No questions. This stuff is obviously something special. They better make it worth our while.

There's more to this whole Mastite thing than we're being told. Yesterday, one of the crew was about to grab a chunk he had found. In the blink of an eye, some sort of energy ball flew out of it and blasted the poor guy back about 100 paces.
What does the Chamber's healer do? Gives him a measly potion! Why are we waiting until the damage is done? We need defensive mages! But somehow, that's out of the question for the Empyrean...
I've calmed down enough to write a coherent letter to the Chamber requesting the resources we need. Now we just have to wait. In the meantime, we'll continue exploring as carefully as possible.

The Chamber finally gave their response. They did send a few mages, but not nearly enough. There's a promise of a larger gold share when the excavation is complete. Somehow, I don't think Empyrean politics will allow such a thing to manifest.
These ruins are larger than we had imagined. There must be other connections to the surface. Krolan found a portal today, but no one dared to enter.
We asked the mages to try analyzing it. Unfortunately, they reported not being able to see through to the other side.

It's finally over! We reached a massive chamber inhabited by a giant antlion! The mages were able to hold it back while we grabbed everything that wasn't nailed down. Thought we were trapped when we had to barricade the gate. Thank the heavens that the portal brought us back here.
A few of the guys were still working on the floor above and didn't follow us into the chamber. We'll head back down and rendezvous with them tomorrow.

When we returned today, the layout of the first floor did not match our maps. Thankfully, an Empyrean mage made it back with us. I asked them to try sensing for human life on the lower levels. Zero results thus far, but I still have hope.

The Chamber sees the situation differently. Orders came in for operations to be moved to other nearby sites. Krolan obeyed. Said he didn't want end up dead like "those guys". As if our guys are dead! When I find them, we're going to snag the rest of that Mastite for ourselves!

Empyrean, the city in the sky. It is a majestic fortress and the last bastion of humankind.
At the height of the kingdom's power the city was a beacon of peace and law.
When darkness invaded the world in the last age people abandoned the surface. Empyrean was their only refuge.
Now the Age of Humanity is ending. Empyrean is crumbling. Scarcity and political infighting have consumed the city.
Some, in desperation, flee to the surface hoping to survive without the protection of the city.
But no one returns from the surface. Most die or go missing. A few hide and survive, for a while.
Surface dwellers cling to hope. Hope that they'll return to Empyrean some day. Hope that a hero will fight back against the darkness.
There is always hope. But not for everyone: not for you. Not for the Exiled.
At long last, your journey across the surface and into the Underworld has come to an end.
Upon entering The Pit, a glowing obelisk shined in the distance.
Guarding the obelisk was Lezaith, a formidable opponent, yet no match for Exiled who faced her.
With Lezaith's defeat, the path to the obelisk was clear.
Not a moment after Lezaith crumbles into a pile of bones, a bolt of lightning strikes the obelisk.
Did Lezaith cast a spell on the obelisk with her dying breath? Had Empyrean finally collapsed?
Maybe it's true what they say. No one returns from the surface. Most die or go missing. A few hide and survive, for a while.

The Book of the Dead tells of redemption for those who sign their name in gravebloom ink. Your sins will be washed away, and you will be able to return to wherever you were banished from.
So, where can I find gravebloom ink?

source_text: The ritual is complete. The Underworld is open to you.
There was a portal to the Underworld in the Wizard's Tower. I shall return there.
If you plan on venturing further, you'll need to learn how to use the resources that you come across.
I can show you how to mix potions, but I don't have any ingredients on hand.
Can I ask you to procure some elements for me? I require one each of the following: Aloe Vera, Mana Crystal, and Mushrooms.
Then return to me with these items, and I will make it worth your time.
Have you gotten those ingredients yet?
Here are the ingredients you asked for.

source_text: Thank you. I was able to find some Aloe Vera on my own, so you can keep what you found.

source_text: Also, take these empty bottles along with this mortar and pestle. You can use the mortar and pestle with that Aloe Vera you found to make a fine healing potion.

source_text: If you ever lose that mortar and pestle, you can always speak to me if you want some potions made.

source_text: You there! I need your help. I'm the last of my group, and want nothing more than to leave this place.
Yet I have one remaining task. I wish to visit the graves of my three fallen partners one last time.
To my disadvantage, their bodies have been taken by the soil here. They tried to attack me when I got near.
If you can prove to me that they are free from their cursed form, I will be in your debt.
I can't assist you myself, but I can offer some of my wares.
Indeed, these items belonged to my companions. I want you to take this as a reward.

source_text: Welcome to the lands of the exiled. Allow me to go over a few things. Click on the arrow to continue.
Your health, mana, and experience points are displayed in the top left of the screen.
In the top right is a map of your current location.

In addition, you can access the Character, Inventory, Powers, and Log menus from the action bar.

Greetings stranger. It's not often that we have people come here from the west.

source_text: One of our encampment's residents, Krolan, works in the nearby mines. He supplies me with various gems that I craft into jewelery.
context: npc_name=Udana, Metalworker; utterance_role=npc; requires_not_status=emp_krolan_init; requires_not_status=emp_krolan_finish; set_status=emp_krolan_init

source_text: Krolan has not returned in some time, and I am starting to think the worst.
context: npc_name=Udana, Metalworker; utterance_role=npc; requires_not_status=emp_krolan_init; requires_not_status=emp_krolan_finish; set_status=emp_krolan_init

source_text: Could you please travel to the mines and look for Krolan? I will find some way to reward you for your trouble.
context: npc_name=Udana, Metalworker; utterance_role=npc; requires_not_status=emp_krolan_init; requires_not_status=emp_krolan_finish; set_status=emp_krolan_init

source_text: This is terrible news. Our camp is already small, so this is a devastating loss.
context: npc_name=Udana, Metalworker; utterance_role=npc; requires_status=emp_krolan_init; requires_status=emp_krolan_emerald; requires_item=1000:1,1001:1; set_status=emp_krolan_finish; unset_status=emp_krolan_init; unset_status=emp_krolan_key; unset_status=emp_krolan_emerald

source_text: If it's any solace, I have his key and this emerald. Mementos to remember him by.
context: npc_name=Udana, Metalworker; utterance_role=player; requires_status=emp_krolan_init; requires_status=emp_krolan_emerald; requires_item=1000:1,1001:1; set_status=emp_krolan_finish; unset_status=emp_krolan_init; unset_status=emp_krolan_key; unset_status=emp_krolan_emerald

context: npc_name=Udana, Metalworker; utterance_role=player; requires_status=emp_krolan_finish; requires_not_status=emp_il_entrance_key; set_status=emp_il_entrance_key

source_text: It was a mining operation. Krolan was a part of the crew.
context: npc_name=Udana, Metalworker; utterance_role=npc; requires_status=emp_krolan_finish; requires_not_status=emp_il_entrance_key; set_status=emp_il_entrance_key

source_text: Not long into their dig, they encountered ruins. Ruins unlike any of the structures in this region.
context: npc_name=Udana, Metalworker; utterance_role=npc; requires_status=emp_krolan_finish; requires_not_status=emp_il_entrance_key; set_status=emp_il_entrance_key

source_text: Amongst these ruins, the crew found an incredible glowing mineral: Mastite.
context: npc_name=Udana, Metalworker; utterance_role=npc; requires_status=emp_krolan_finish; requires_not_status=emp_il_entrance_key; set_status=emp_il_entrance_key

source_text: When the Empyrean caught wind of this discovery, they promptly took control of the operation.
context: npc_name=Udana, Metalworker; utterance_role=npc; requires_status=emp_krolan_finish; requires_not_status=emp_il_entrance_key; set_status=emp_il_entrance_key

source_text: So why is it blocked off now? Did the Empyrean strip it clean?
context: npc_name=Udana, Metalworker; utterance_role=player; requires_status=emp_krolan_finish; requires_not_status=emp_il_entrance_key; set_status=emp_il_entrance_key

source_text: The further the excavation team dug, the more apparent it became that something was unusual about the ruins. North would become south, west would become east. They were losing workers.
context: npc_name=Udana, Metalworker; utterance_role=npc; requires_status=emp_krolan_finish; requires_not_status=emp_il_entrance_key; set_status=emp_il_entrance_key

source_text: The Empyrean shut down the operation. Instead, they made an effort to mine other nearby areas in hope of finding a more stable source of Mastite. You've already seen the futile end to that story.
context: npc_name=Udana, Metalworker; utterance_role=npc; requires_status=emp_krolan_finish; requires_not_status=emp_il_entrance_key; set_status=emp_il_entrance_key

source_text: If the Empyrean gave up on the ruins, there may still be some value in exploring it. Is there any way I can get inside?
context: npc_name=Udana, Metalworker; utterance_role=player; requires_status=emp_krolan_finish; requires_not_status=emp_il_entrance_key; set_status=emp_il_entrance_key

source_text: It's risky, but you proven that you're able to handle yourself. And maybe if we can gain our own supply of Mastite, we'll have some leverage against the Empyrean.
context: npc_name=Udana, Metalworker; utterance_role=npc; requires_status=emp_krolan_finish; requires_not_status=emp_il_entrance_key; set_status=emp_il_entrance_key

source_text: Here. I made a copy of the key you'll need after one of the Empyrean guards dropped it. Please be careful. I'm not sure I'm ready to be exposed to any more death.
context: npc_name=Udana, Metalworker; utterance_role=npc; requires_status=emp_krolan_finish; requires_not_status=emp_il_entrance_key; set_status=emp_il_entrance_key

source_text: It was a mining operation. Krolan was a part of the crew.
Not long into their dig, they encountered ruins. Ruins unlike any of the structures in this region.
Amongst these ruins, the crew found an incredible glowing mineral: Mastite.
When the Empyrean caught wind of this discovery, they promptly took control of the operation.
The further the excavation team dug, the more apparent it became that something was unusual about the ruins. North would become south, west would become east. They were losing workers.
The Empyrean shut down the operation. Instead, they made an effort to mine other nearby areas in hope of finding a more stable source of Mastite. You've already seen the futile end to that story.
Thank you again for your help.
